mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during the same month, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns fail to outperform the 30-day moving average during the same employment expansion period, or monthly PAYEMS growth <10,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy (HOUST) below 90 and 500, respectively, indicates weakening overall economic momentum, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar dual-signal events, or INDPRO and HOUST recover above thresholds within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month predicts supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and compressing S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the same INDPRO contraction month (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4%, monetary policy shifts toward easing, lowering real rates and supporting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are flat or negative during the UNRATE <4% period compared to the prior 10-day average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales proxy (implied via RSAFS > 350,000) indicates consumer confidence, which elevates earnings forecasts and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS exceeds 350,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns underperform the 30-day average during the RSAFS expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 237 and industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 suggests inflationary pressure with weak demand, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of similar dual-signal events over the past 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the GDP deflator (implied via CPIAUCSL > 240 for three months) suggests persistent cost pressures, which elevates uncertainty and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains above 240 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically negative during the CPIAUCSL >240 period (p > 0.05).
